title: Relative boundary filling for symmetric operadic extension families
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces, degreewise simplicial pullbacks and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], symmetric infinity-operads and inert-preserving maps of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], and the active concatenation $\oplus$ of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation]. Let $q:\mathcal E^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ be a cocartesian fibration and a map of symmetric infinity-operads. Let $\mathcal P^\otimes\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal Q^\otimes\to\mathcal O^\otimes$ be maps of small symmetric infinity-operads. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_{/\mathcal O^\otimes}(\mathcal P^\otimes,\mathcal E^\otimes)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_{/\mathcal O^\otimes}(\mathcal Q^\otimes,\mathcal E^\otimes)$: the full subcategories on inert-preserving functors, with all coherent transformations over $\mathcal O^\otimes$. Restriction is $u^*:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$. The coherent comma quasicategory $\mathcal T$ of triples $(A,F,\eta:A\to u^*F)$ is modeled by
$$\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal A)\times_{\mathcal A,\operatorname{ev}_1,u^*}\mathcal B,$$
with source projection $r:\mathcal T\to\mathcal A$ given by $\operatorname{ev}_0$. Its simplices retain the whole coherent family of these arrows and both endpoint algebra functors.

For a vertex $H=(A,F,\eta)$ and a color $d$ of $\mathcal Q$, put $J_d=\mathcal P^\otimes\times_{\mathcal Q^\otimes}(\mathcal Q^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})_{/d}$ and let $D_d:J_d\to\mathcal E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ be $A$ after source projection. The transformation $\eta$ and the arrows into $d$ induce an active coherent cocone $c_d:D_d\to\Delta_{J_d}F(d)$ with component $F(\alpha)\eta_p$ at $(p,\alpha:u(p)\to d)$. Say that $H$ satisfies the local condition if for every $d$, every $Z\in\mathcal E^\otimes$ and every $W\in\mathcal E^\otimes_{\langle1\rangle}$, restriction along $c_d\oplus1_Z$ gives a homotopy pullback square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}}(F(d)\oplus Z,W)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J_d,\mathcal E^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})}(D_d\oplus Z,\Delta_{J_d}W)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal O^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}}(q(F(d)\oplus Z),qW)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J_d,\mathcal O^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})}(q(D_d\oplus Z),\Delta_{J_d}(qW)).
\end{array}$$
Here the vertical maps apply $q$ and the bottom map uses the specified base cocone $qc_d$; a homotopy pullback means equivalence with the path-space homotopy fiber product, retaining its specified composition homotopy. This is the mapping-space form of the operadic relative colimit condition, tested after every fixed concatenation; it is a condition on the given cocones, with no existence assertion.

For every $n>0$, suppose $b:\Delta^n\to\mathcal A$ and $h_0:\partial\Delta^n\to\mathcal T$ satisfy $rh_0=b|_{\partial\Delta^n}$ exactly, and the vertex $h_0(0)$ satisfies the local condition. Then there exists $h:\Delta^n\to\mathcal T$ with $rh=b$ and $h|_{\partial\Delta^n}=h_0$ exactly. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ is the union of the proper faces of the standard simplex. No terminal-object, presentability or global colimit hypothesis is imposed.
